text_en: Two memorandums were signed one on trade facilitation and movement of persons, the second on steps towards a single labour market.
summary: Albania, North Macedonia and Serbia signed two memorandums: on trade facilitation and movement of persons, and on steps towards a single labour market.
note: Regional labour mobility of nationals, outside the Chapter 2 boundary (G5-D06).

text_en: A number of important decisions to facilitate the movement of workers remain blocked.
summary: A number of important decisions to facilitate the movement of workers remain blocked.
note: Regional labour mobility of nationals, outside the Chapter 2 boundary (G5-D06).

text_en: During 2024 the activities on implementation/application of facilitated access to the labour market within the Open Balkan Initiative (between RS Macedonia, Serbia and Albania) were also carried out, and the service for free access to the labour market between the 3 states began from March 2024.
summary: Free labour-market access between North Macedonia, Serbia and Albania under the Open Balkan Initiative began as a service from March 2024.
note: Regional labour mobility of nationals, outside the Chapter 2 boundary (G5-D06).

text_en: During 2024, 120 registrations in compulsory social insurance (M1) with an Open Balkan certificate were carried out.
summary: In 2024, 120 M1 compulsory social insurance registrations were made with an Open Balkan certificate.
note: Regional labour mobility of nationals, outside the Chapter 2 boundary (G5-D06).

text_en: As part of the initiative, several memoranda, agreements and common declarations have been signed so far, among which the Memorandum of Cooperation related to the free access to the labor market in the Western Balkans, through reduced employment barriers among the countries, electronic application for obtaining identification number and facilitation of administrative procedures for obtaining a temporary residence per
summary: Under the Open Balkan Initiative a memorandum was signed on free labour market access, including electronic application for an identification number and simpler residence procedures.
note: Regional labour mobility of nationals, outside the Chapter 2 boundary (G5-D06).

text_en: It stipulates that every resident of the signatory countries has the right to free movement, residence and work in the territory of the three countries. In order to ensure equal access for all residents of these countries, the signatories should simplify the procedures for entry, residence and work in their countries.
summary: The memorandum gives residents of the signatory countries the right to move, reside and work in all three, and obliges signatories to simplify procedures.
note: Regional labour mobility of nationals, outside the Chapter 2 boundary (G5-D06).

text_en: Before or at the latest 90 days after entering of the neighboring country, residents of the contracting countries should register in order to obtain a permit for free access to the labor market for a period of two years, with the possibility of its extension. The permit includes the right to employment without a work and residence permit for foreign nationals, but excludes the possibility of using state subsidies for
summary: Residents must register within 90 days for a two-year renewable labour market access permit, without work or residence permits, excluding state employment subsidies.
note: Regional labour mobility of nationals, outside the Chapter 2 boundary (G5-D06).

text_en: Whether simplified employment rules in these countries under the OBI umbrella will make them more attractive than EU countries depends on the wage levels in the destination country as the most significant factor affecting labor mobility..
summary: Whether simpler Open Balkan employment rules make these countries more attractive than EU countries depends on destination wage levels.
note: Regional labour mobility of nationals, outside the Chapter 2 boundary (G5-D06).

text_en: As the Open Balkan Initiative is a three-lateral project of North Macedonia, Serbia and Albania, it is expected that the planning regions bordering the other two countries would benefit the most of the initiative for free labor mobility.
summary: The planning regions bordering Serbia and Albania are expected to benefit most from the Open Balkan free labour mobility initiative.
note: Regional labour mobility of nationals, outside the Chapter 2 boundary (G5-D06).

text_en: However, the estimated wage differentials for these occupations are statistically insignificant, suggesting that we cannot expect an increased inflow of Serbian workers who would fulfil the shortage of workers in North Macedonia.
summary: Wage differentials for these occupations are insignificant, so no increased inflow of Serbian workers to fill shortages is expected.
note: Regional labour mobility of nationals, outside the Chapter 2 boundary (G5-D06).

text_en: Medium-skilled service and sales workers are paid more in North Macedonia, especially personal care workers who receive almost 50% higher wages than workers in Serbia. The Open Balkan initiative can result in greater mobility of these workers from Serbia to North Macedonia, hence reducing their shortage.
summary: Service and sales workers, especially personal care workers, earn more in North Macedonia; the Initiative may draw them from Serbia, reducing shortages.
note: Regional labour mobility of nationals, outside the Chapter 2 boundary (G5-D06).

text_en: However, the previous estimations showed that in North Macedonia, there is deficit of building workers only, and the higher salary of 9.5% can, to a certain extent, encourage Serbian workers to relocate in North Macedonia.
summary: Building workers, the only craft occupation in deficit, earn 9.5% more in North Macedonia, which may encourage Serbian workers to relocate.
note: Regional labour mobility of nationals, outside the Chapter 2 boundary (G5-D06).

text_en: The positive wage differentials for all low-skill occupations are encouraging, hinting that higher wages in North Macedonia may attract workers from Serbia, who will fill the significant shortage of these workers.
summary: Higher low-skill wages in North Macedonia may attract Serbian workers to fill significant shortages.
note: Regional labour mobility of nationals, outside the Chapter 2 boundary (G5-D06).

text_en: IT professional and technicians in the borderline regions of North Macedonia receive 37% and 21.6% higher wages, respectively, although the national data showed a reverse trend. This is probably driven by the higher wages that IT companies in the Skopje region pay, and may cause a significant inflow of Serbian IT workers from the borderline places to the IT companies based in Skopje.
summary: IT professionals and technicians in border regions earn 37% and 21.6% more, which may cause a significant inflow of Serbian IT workers.
note: Regional labour mobility of nationals, outside the Chapter 2 boundary (G5-D06).

text_en: The need for customer care clerks in the Skopje region is high; 68 workers are needed for each job vacancy. At the same time, the wage for these workers in the borderline regions in the county is 17.7% higher in North Macedonia, opening the possibility of attracting workers from Serbia.
summary: Customer care clerks are in high demand in Skopje and earn 17.7% more in border regions, possibly attracting workers from Serbia.
note: Regional labour mobility of nationals, outside the Chapter 2 boundary (G5-D06).

text_en: The Initiative, as an opportunity for regional economic integration with our neighbors, is extremely important for the Macedonian economy and should enable a faster structural adjustment to the challenges brought by the open labor market. The Initiative’s effect on the domestic labor market depends on its current state, but also on the desire of policymakers to conduct structural changes.
summary: The Open Balkan Initiative is very important for the economy; its labour market effect depends on current conditions and policymakers' will for structural change.
note: Regional labour mobility of nationals, outside the Chapter 2 boundary (G5-D06).

text_en: Seen from the perspective of the regional integration and labor mobility, the advantages of the OBI would be fulfilling the shortages of workers, especially in the borderline regions.
summary: From a mobility perspective, the Open Balkan Initiative's advantage would be filling worker shortages, especially in border regions.
note: Regional labour mobility of nationals, outside the Chapter 2 boundary (G5-D06).

text_en: The OBI needs to be a stimulus for faster conduct of the structural reforms for addressing the existing labor market gaps and a starting point in the eventual opening of the labor market upon accession to the EU.
summary: The Open Balkan Initiative should speed structural labour market reforms and prepare for opening the labour market upon EU accession.
note: Regional labour mobility of nationals, outside the Chapter 2 boundary (G5-D06).
